_about: Every statement the game makes about what the novel says or does. A fact or reading carries a passage that must be in the 1897 text (claims/source/dracula-1897.txt, Project Gutenberg #345) in the chapter named; case, quotation marks and dashes are ignored. An absence claim (the novel never does X) cannot be shown by a passage: it lists terms that must not occur anywhere in the text, and says what else supports it. `where` names the ending or scene of either seat that relies on it. Checked by `npm run check:claims`.

absences.claim: The Count never travels with a household to Antwerp or anywhere else.
absences.support: To be confirmed by a reader who knows the book: he leaves England alone on the Czarina Catherine with one box (ch 24, 26). The word Antwerp occurs once, in a telegram of Van Helsing's.

absences.claim: London is never put under fog for days by the Count.
absences.support: To be confirmed by a reader who knows the book: the fog and mist he raises are local and brief.

absences.claim: The Count never makes a stand at Carfax.
absences.support: To be confirmed by a reader who knows the book: the hunters sanctify the boxes at Carfax and the Count is not there (ch 19).

absences.claim: The Count never carries Mina with him to the pass.
absences.support: To be confirmed by a reader who knows the book: Mina travels with Van Helsing (ch 26, 27).
